Prepare a wide variety of recipes from around the world, and hype them up to earn extra praise! In Diced Veggies you take turns with the cleaver, slicing ingredient dice away from the shared chopping block and assigning them to the recipes you’re working on. This unique resource-gathering mechanism is the key to your scrumptious success. The particular veggies that your recipes require isn't your only consideration... you can only take a limited number of pips with each chop, and the right dice values can unlock all sorts of drool-worthy Hypes to boost a recipe's score! A clever cleaver is all you need to whip up delicious recipes in this dice-slicing game for up to four chefs! Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary You must use the cleaver to make one cut that separates one or more dice from the block. Lower it carefully into the seam beside the dice you want to cut away, then push the blade gently sideways to separate the dice from the block. Do not disturb the dice numbers when you cut. If the block gets messy, tidy it up. Gather your dice, without disturbing their numbers… it’s best to slide them instead of picking them up! The numbers on the dice you push must have a combined total of 10 or lower. If all dice in the block have a combined pip total of 10 or lower, simply take them all without cutting. The block must be in one piece when you are done; no portions disconnected or touching only by a corner. Note that the dice do not have ones and are instead 2-2-3-4-5-6. If you have all of the ingredients displayed on any of your Recipes, you can cook! Each die counts as one ingredient of its type. •You may cook more than one Recipe per turn. •You don’t have to cook, even if you could. To cook, show everyone that you’ve got the right dice, then discard them into the frame. Flip your cooked Recipes face down. Don’t stack them; everyone needs to know how many Recipes you have completed. HYPE CARDS When you cook a Recipe, you may also play a Hype from your hand (one per Recipe). Each Hype describes its requirements for playing it. Keep your Hypes in mind when cutting! Read it aloud to confirm that you have met its requirements before discarding your dice. Keep your scored Hypes paired face down with their Recipes; sometimes during scoring you need to know which one goes with which. CHEF TOKEN Before you cook, you may discard your Chef token to change either the type or the number of one of your dice. You’ll get your Chef token back whenever anyone Restocks (see Restocking, below), so don’t be too cautious about using it! Step 3 : Card Draw one card; a Hype from the deck, or a Recipe (from the deck or from the display). •If you draw a Recipe from the display, fill the gap with a new one drawn from the deck. Ending turn At the end of your turn, you may keep (at most) eight dice, two Recipes and two Hypes. If you are over limit in any category, you must discard items of your choice until you are within the limits. Discarded dice go into the frame. Discarded cards go into separate discard piles; if either deck ever runs out, shuffle the discards to form a new deck. Restocking When your turn starts if there is at least one ingredient type missing from the block, you may choose to Restock. If there are no dice left in the block, you must Restock. To Restock: Place the frame back in the middle of the table. Return all spent Chef tokens to their owners. Gather all spent dice, and all leftover dice from the block (players keep all of their unspent dice). Roll them loosely into the frame. Drag the frame diagonally so that all of the dice settle into a corner, forming a partially-complete block that is still neatly aligned in rows and columns. [Rating: 1/10] Too limiting and too sluggishly paced for a game that should be much quicker. A lot of that has to do with the dice "cutting" mechanic, which sounds fine at a glance but is a nightmare in practice. I understand some limitation on the number of acquired dice must be enforced; however, the limit of total face value 10 or less is too restrictive. Most turns you're taking two dice. Sometimes only one. Rarely three or more. Recipes thus can become a chore to complete and the bonus cards are twice as annoying to fulfill. "Complete a recipe with all value 2 dice." [Rating: 1/10] Don't like the art nor the design nor the restrictive options. Many other games of this type to play.

[Rating: 3/10] Way below average. I get why it's gonna be fun for some, but it's almost too casual, and the gimmick is, surprisingly, not actually that cute in practice. It's crazy forgettable and also manages to not work with the gimmick in a way that feels completely devoid of choice.

[Rating: 3/10] Cute game with a cute theme.  There's not a lot of cards seen, and some luck with the Hype cards.  Not that I mind, it's a short game that doesn't wear out its welcome.

[Rating: 3/10] As a medium light gamer...i really cannot recommend this game.  We tried in every player count, and none of the people I played with likes it. We even tried it with 5 players one time and everyone are bored on the first few round and we have to stop the game.  It is really sad for me. I enjoy KTBG games a lot. I love contract fulfilling and bonus point in games. The art looks gorgeous. While everything on paper sounds amazing, the gameplay is just not matching that energy.   I really tried and it honestly bored me every time. I feel sorry but its not a game for me and my friends.

[Rating: 3/10] After 1 play on BGA: I was surprised by how little this game interested me. The theme – vegetables and delicious dishes – is actually quite appealing to me. But the dice drafting felt sluggish and unexciting. Assigning the painstakingly drafted dice to the dishes was just as tedious. Overall, it felt like a game designed by an AI that never tested whether real people would actually enjoy playing it. More likely, though, it simply doesn’t align with my personal taste.

[Rating: 3.5/10] Great idea that's wrapped in a boring contract fulfillment mechanic. Nothing really wrong, but this could be taken to a much better game space. Doing your first recipe is okay, but nothing exciting. And then you do it again 5 more times, which gets tedious. There's just no build up or excitement generated by the game.

[Rating: 4/10] Simple game, might be good for counting with kids, but I didn't feel like I really had any interesting choices throughout the game.

[Rating: 4/10] While this is a cute game the cards and dice not meshing make it a futile attempt at winning far too often. No mitigation of the terrible setup at the start with the dice rolling and you have to hope you have cards that match while fighting over ingredients if the dice aren't too high to even cut. That can't be over 10 limit makes it take waaaaay too much effort to get them. Hype cards are even worse as they can be completely worthless to add any bonus points with. It's far too luck dependent overall. End game conditions hit and then no one can usually do anything, making it seem very unfinish
